newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Eurofighter vital for Germany.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Eurofighter vital for Germany.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that building the Eurofighter combat aircraft was vital for Germany's defence, and added that he expected Germany to commit itself to the project.
Waigel made no comments on talks earlier in the day with Manfred Bischoff, chief executive of Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, on completing financing for the 180 Eurofighters Germany wants to buy.
But, asked whether Germany would build the Eurofighter, he answered: "I believe so, yes."

"I believe that it (the Eurofighter) is absolutely necessary for our defence," Waigel told reporters. "This is an international project where, in my opinion, Germany must not lose the confidence" of its partners.
Waigel is trying to close a financing gap of two billion marks ($1.2 billion) to pay for the 180 Eurofighters Germany need to modernise its airforce for the 21st century.

Waigel was negotiating with Bischoff over the return of one billion marks in prefinancing loans granted for Dasa's Airbus civilian aircraft operations. The other billion marks is expected to come from Defence Minister Volker Ruehe's departmental budget.
Ruehe told reporters that negotiations over Eurofighter financing as well as the 1998 defence budget were still continuing.

He added that the government was working on putting together solid financing for the armed forces and for large defence procurement contracts like Eurofighter, and he ruled out any reduction in the size of Germany's Eurofighter order.

Eurofighter partners include DASA, a unit of carmaker Daimler-Benz AG, with British Aerospace, Alenia of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain. German financing has held up Eurofighter orders form Italy and Spain, while Britain has approved orders for 232 aircraft.
